newsitem.title: CHINA: Rate cuts put billions of yuan into China stocks.
newsitem.headline: Rate cuts put billions of yuan into China stocks.

text.p: Two cuts in bank interest rates this year has slowed the growth in individual bank deposits in Shanghai and diverted tens of billions of yuan into the stock market, the Shanghai Securities News said on Monday.
The central bank cut interest rates in May and August.

In the second quarter of this year bank deposits rose 3.63 billion yuan over the same 1995 period and in July and August by an average of 1.53 billion yuan a month over 1995, the newspaper said. In the first quarter, Shanghai's individual bank deposits rose 6.39 billion yuan year on year.
It said the volume in current accounts as a proportion of total deposits rose after the rate cuts. With the cut in rates, several tens of billions of yuan flowed into the stock markets.

In the first eight months of this year, turnover on the Shanghai stock market was 1.318 trillion yuan, compared to 546.2 billion for the whole of 1995, excluding last year's trading in treasury bill futures which was banned, the newspaper said.
Between January and March, average monthly trading volume was 44 billion yuan and from April to August it was 237.2 billion yuan, it said.
Between January and August, 62 new companies were listed on the Shanghai exchange, the newspaper added.
